main.old_effective_key: f"Reinhard Kneser and Hermann Ney's smoothing, from 1995, has two ideas. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, absolute discounting: shave the fixed discount off every count you've seen, <bookmark mark='c'/> and use the savings to back off to a shorter context, one character fewer: blend the two. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second, judge the shorter contexts by their variety. In the novels, '{d['word']}' appears {d['word_count']:,} times, but its number of distinct predecessors is {d['word_prev']}; its most common predecessor is '{d['word_top_prev']}'. '{d['other']}' is about as common, and follows {d['other_prev']:,} different words. <bookmark mark='d'/> After an unfamiliar word, '{d['other']}' is the far better guess. So the shorter contexts count how many different contexts something follows, not how often it appears."

main.Chinese: 赖因哈德·克内泽和赫尔曼·奈1995年的平滑法有两个想法。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一，绝对折扣：每个见过的计数都削去一个固定的折扣，<bookmark mark='c'/>把省下来的概率交给少一个字符的短上下文，把两者混合。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二，用多样性判断短上下文。在小说里，‘{d['word']}’出现了{d['word_count']:,}次，却只有{d['word_prev']}种不同的前驱；最常见的前驱是‘{d['word_top_prev']}’。‘{d['other']}’差不多常见，却跟在{d['other_prev']:,}种不同的词后面。<bookmark mark='d'/>{continuation}所以短上下文数的是一个东西跟在多少种不同上下文后面，不是它总共出现多少次。

main.Chinese: 通过在同一段验证后缀上比较阶数，选出{k['best']}个字符的上下文后，Kneser–Ney跳过评分段落最前面的{k['best']}个字符，达到每字符{k['best_bits']:.2f}比特。这个基准保留所选阶数自己的评分起点，与接下来的无穷元比较一致。<bookmark mark='a'/>有二十年，从语音识别到机器翻译，有噪信道里的语言模型都是Kneser–Ney这一类。斯坦利·陈和乔舒亚·古德曼1998年的细致比较发现，在他们测试的方法里，一种改进版Kneser–Ney表现最好。但为什么要停在{k['best']}个字符呢？
